models.section: Basic Model: contact-phase force, loss, and takeoff energy
models.purpose: Map half-pipe geometry and rider path to normal force, accumulated snow/air loss, human work, and takeoff kinetic state.
models.summary: The paper inventories gravity, normal force, snow friction, and quadratic air resistance; projects the normal force on an extruded path; integrates losses; solves a linear loss ODE; and adds stand-up work at the coping.

variables.definition: Independent coordinate across the half-pipe cross-section.
Cross-section elevation as a function of x.
Downhill coordinate of the rider path as a function of x.
Normal force of the snow on the rider.
Mechanical energy lost to snow friction and air drag up to x.
Coefficient multiplying normal force in the snow-friction law.
Coefficient multiplying squared speed in the resistance model as printed.
Work added when the rider stands up by height Delta h at the coping.
Speed immediately before the fly.

governing_equations.source_expression: f = alpha N + beta(xdot^2 + ydot^2 + zdot^2); alpha N + beta(1+y'^2+z'^2)xdot^2
governing_equations.normalized_latex: f=\alpha N+\beta(\dot x^2+\dot y^2+\dot z^2)=\alpha N+\beta(1+y'^2+z'^2)\dot x^2
governing_equations.purpose: Combine snow friction and air resistance along the path.

governing_equations.source_expression: rho = (1+y'^2)^(3/2)/y''; N = m xdot^2/rho + mg cos theta/sqrt(1+y'^2) = (y'' xdot^2 + g cos theta)m/sqrt(1+y'^2)
governing_equations.purpose: Express curvature radius and projected normal force.

governing_equations.source_expression: ds = sqrt(1+y'^2+z'^2) dx
governing_equations.purpose: Define the three-dimensional path-length differential.

governing_equations.source_expression: 1/2 m(1+y'^2+z'^2) xdot^2 = E0 - E_lost - mg(y cos theta - z sin theta)
governing_equations.purpose: Balance kinetic energy with initial energy, losses, and gravitational potential.

governing_equations.source_expression: xdot^2 = 2/[m(1+y'^2+z'^2)] [E0-E_lost-mg(y cos theta-z sin theta)]
governing_equations.purpose: Solve the energy balance for squared cross-section speed.

governing_equations.source_expression: E_lost(x)=integral_0^x f ds = integral_0^x {alpha N sqrt(1+y'^2+z'^2)+beta(1+y'^2+z'^2)xdot^2} dtau, followed by a substituted form
governing_equations.purpose: Accumulate friction and air-drag work along the path before substitution.

governing_equations.source_expression: E_lost = exp(-integral_x0^x a(tau)d tau) [integral_x0^x b(tau) exp(integral_x0^tau a(sigma)d sigma)d tau]
governing_equations.purpose: State the integrating-factor solution of the linear loss ODE.
Define the coefficient multiplying accumulated loss in the linear ODE.

governing_equations.source_expression: b(x)= (2 alpha y''/((1+y'^2)sqrt(1+y'^2+z'^2))+2 beta/m)[E0-mg(y cos theta-z sin theta)] + alpha mg cos theta sqrt((1+y'^2+z'^2)/(1+y'^2))
governing_equations.purpose: Define the forcing term in the loss ODE.

governing_equations.source_expression: W_human = y_t'^2/[1+y_t'^2+z_t'^2] m Delta h
governing_equations.purpose: Approximate the vertical component of stand-up work at the edge.

equation_status.reason: Equations (1)-(10) were visually checked on rendered pages 7-8; the long substituted loss expression is retained at formula-family level with medium transcription confidence.

objectives: Minimize accumulated loss and determine takeoff energy for a given course and path.
constraints: Downward-convex almost-everywhere C2 cross-section
Prescribed course y(x) and rider path z(x)
Baseline crouch and discrete stand-up action

details: E_lost(x0)=0 is implicit in the integrating-factor form; E0 is the cycle-start mechanical energy.
The path starts at one coping and reaches the opposite takeoff edge.
The model follows a transient traversal rather than an equilibrium.

parameter_estimation.method: alpha, beta, mass, slope, and E0 are assembled from references and a drop-in calculation rather than jointly fitted.

steps: compute stand-up work and takeoff speed
algorithm.convergence_criteria: No solver, discretization, tolerance, or convergence test is reported.

assumptions: Snow friction is proportional to normal force.
Air resistance is proportional to squared speed.
The board force acts at its center.
Environmental and detailed board mechanics are omitted.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The two loss coefficients and initial energy are sourced or hand-computed; no data set independently identifies their combined effects.

validation_refs: Page 16 plausibility comparison and local sensitivity table
models.computational_cost: A one-dimensional numerical calculus/ODE evaluation is asserted, but mesh size and run cost are omitted.
strengths: Connects geometry, path, forces, loss, and athlete work in one explicit chain.
limitations: The printed drag-work simplification drops a three-dimensional path factor.
The initial-energy slope calculation later uses cosine rather than sine.
missing_details: units and calibration evidence for every parameter

models.section: Basic Model: projectile flight and repeated-cycle energy
models.family: projectile motion with optional drag and energy handoff
models.purpose: Convert the takeoff state into vertical air, airtime, downhill displacement, and next-cycle energy.
models.summary: The paper derives a no-drag vertical-air formula, a scalar drag variant, flight duration and distance, gravitational change, and a repeated-cycle energy relation.

variables.definition: Maximum vertical distance above the coping during flight.
Duration of the airborne phase.
Displacement in the downhill z direction during flight.
Kinetic energy at the end of the fly and start energy for the next cycle.
Takeoff velocity component used in the height and time formulas.
Quadratic drag coefficient reused during flight.

governing_equations.source_expression: 1/2 m(y_t'^2+z_t'^2) = E0-E_lost(x_t)+mg z_t sin theta + [y_t'^2/(1+y_t'^2+z_t'^2)]m Delta h
governing_equations.purpose: Balance energy at the takeoff edge.

governing_equations.source_expression: y_t^2 = 2/[m(1+(z_t'/y_t')^2)] [E0-E_lost(x_t)+mg z_t sin theta + y_t'^2/(1+y_t'^2+z_t'^2)m Delta h]
governing_equations.purpose: Solve the takeoff balance for the velocity component used as vertical.

governing_equations.source_expression: H_f = [1/(cos^2 theta)] [v_y^2/(2g cos theta)] expressed after substituting equation (12)
governing_equations.purpose: Compute no-drag vertical air from the projected takeoff component.

governing_equations.source_expression: F = beta(ydot^2+zdot^2); yddot = -g cos theta - (beta/m) ydot^2
governing_equations.purpose: Introduce the paper's scalarized flight-drag equation.

governing_equations.source_expression: H_f = m/(2 beta) ln(1 + beta y_t^2/(mg cos theta))
governing_equations.purpose: Compute vertical air under the scalarized quadratic-drag equation.

governing_equations.source_expression: t = 2 v_y/(g cos theta)
governing_equations.purpose: Compute no-drag flight duration.

governing_equations.source_expression: S_f = z_t' t + 1/2 g sin theta t^2; W_G = mg S_f sin theta
governing_equations.purpose: Compute downhill displacement and gravitational potential change during flight.

governing_equations.source_expression: E0 = E_lost + mg z_t sin theta + W_G + W_human + E_reach; E_reach = E0-E_lost-mg z_t sin theta-W_G-W_human
governing_equations.purpose: Hand the terminal flight energy to the next cycle.

equation_status.reason: The flight and cycle equations were visually checked on pages 8-10; equation (13) is retained as printed despite a coordinate-projection concern.

objectives: Maximize vertical air and characterize airtime, flight distance, and retained energy.
constraints: Basic flight returns to the coping
No-drag and scalar-drag cases are treated separately
Slope frame is fixed during flight

details: Initial flight state is the takeoff energy and tangent-velocity ratio from the contact model.
The basic model assumes return at the opposite coping.
Projectile flight is transient.

parameter_estimation.method: The same sourced beta and mass are reused; no flight data are fitted.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: No integrator, event detector, tolerance, or convergence rule is stated.

assumptions: The global takeoff state is inferred from local derivatives.
The drag extension is scalarized.
The basic landing occurs at the coping.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The coordinate transformation and drag law are not validated against flight trajectories, and landing feasibility is imposed rather than solved.

models.computational_cost: Analytic formulas plus an unspecified numerical trajectory simulation.
strengths: Retains the official vertical-air metric and a next-cycle state rather than stopping at takeoff speed.
limitations: The local-to-global velocity projection in equation (13) is not established.
The flight drag component is not the vector quadratic-drag component.
Equations (17)-(18) subtract gravitational gain and athlete work in the next-cycle ledger.

models.section: Basic Model: initial angular momentum and trick interpretation
models.purpose: Relate course curvature and takeoff speed to one initial angular-momentum component and interpret possible rotations.
models.summary: The paper decomposes angular momentum by axis, assigns the z component to course curvature, approximates the rider as a stick, and maps component combinations to twist, flip, cork, and combined tricks.

variables.definition: Initial angular momentum about the paper's z direction.
Stick-model moment of inertia used for Lz0.
Course-tangent rotation rate immediately before takeoff.
Radius of curvature at the edge.
Stick length representing the rider.

governing_equations.source_expression: L_z0 = 1/3 l^2 omega_0 m
governing_equations.purpose: Approximate the initial angular momentum of the rider as a stick.

governing_equations.source_expression: omega_0 = sqrt(x_t^2+y_t^2)/rho_0
governing_equations.purpose: Convert edge speed and curvature to a takeoff angular rate.

governing_equations.source_expression: L_z0 = 1/3 [sqrt(x_t^2+y_t^2)/rho_0] l^2 m
governing_equations.purpose: Combine the stick inertia and edge-curvature rate into the optimization proxy.

equation_status.reason: Equations (19)-(21) were visually checked on page 11.

objectives: Increase course-controlled Lz0 while preserving takeoff energy and feasible curvature.
constraints: Course geometry affects Lz0 only in the paper's allocation
Other angular components are athlete-controlled
Rider is approximated by a stick

details: Angular state is evaluated immediately before takeoff.
rho0 is the curvature radius at the coping edge.
The model concerns an impulse/state at takeoff.

parameter_estimation.method: No body-length, inertia, or angular-momentum calibration protocol is given.

steps: Evaluate the closed-form proxy from takeoff speed and curvature.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Closed-form evaluation; no iterative criterion applies.

assumptions: A one-dimensional stick represents the rider.
Course tangent rotation is transferred to rider body rotation.
The reference point for inertia is not declared.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: No contact torque or angular impulse identifies how course curvature creates rider angular momentum about the center of mass.

validation_refs: Figures 8-11 provide geometric interpretation only; no measured angular momentum is compared.
models.computational_cost: Closed-form evaluation for each candidate geometry.
strengths: Separates course-controlled and athlete-controlled angular components before optimization.
limitations: The end-pivot inertia factor and angular-momentum reference point are unspecified.
Course tangent rotation is treated as rider spin without a torque model.

models.section: Extended Model: athlete path, takeoff, posture, and landing
models.family: behavioral modifications to takeoff and landing
models.purpose: Add athlete-controlled path endpoint, velocity direction, posture change, and landing choice to the objective-factors baseline.
models.summary: The extension compares maintaining vertical speed with redirecting downhill kinetic energy, relates posture to rotation through changing inertia, and discusses coping versus transition landing.

variables.definition: Downhill path coordinate at the takeoff point.
Velocity component the rider may maintain or increase before flight.
Velocity component the rider may reduce before flight.
Total angle accumulated during the airborne phase.
Posture-dependent moment of inertia discussed qualitatively.
Coping or transition landing option.

governing_equations.source_expression: H_f for maintaining y_t repeats the no-drag height expression using E0-E_lost+mg z_t sin theta plus stand-up work
governing_equations.purpose: Represent vertical air when the rider maintains the modeled vertical component.

governing_equations.source_expression: S_f = 1/2 g sin theta (2 v_y/(g cos theta))^2
governing_equations.purpose: Compute downhill flight distance when the downhill takeoff component is reduced.

governing_equations.source_expression: v_y^2 = 2/m [E0-E_lost(x_t)+mg z_t sin theta + y_t'^2/(1+y_t'^2+z_t'^2)m Delta h]
governing_equations.purpose: Assign the available takeoff kinetic energy to the vertical component in the conversion case.

governing_equations.source_expression: H_f = [1/cos^2 theta] [v_y^2/(2g cos theta)] with equation (24) substituted
governing_equations.purpose: Compute vertical air under the full energy-conversion scenario.

governing_equations.source_expression: S_f = 1/2 g sin theta (2 v_y/(g cos theta))^2
governing_equations.purpose: Compute flight distance in the full energy-conversion scenario.

equation_status.reason: Equations (22)-(26) were visually checked on page 17; posture and landing modifications remain qualitative and have no governing equations.

objectives: Increase vertical air or rotation while retaining enough cycles, landing safety, and speed.
constraints: Five to eight tricks/cycles are required in the event
The athlete can alter path and posture
Landing may occur at coping or on the transition

details: The extension begins from the baseline takeoff-energy state.
The chosen landing point is discussed but not solved as a trajectory-surface intersection.
The extension is transient and action-dependent.

parameter_estimation.method: No athlete control, posture schedule, or landing-risk parameters are calibrated.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: No control optimization or landing event solver is reported.

assumptions: A skilled athlete may redirect velocity components.
Angular momentum is conserved in air while inertia can change.
Transition landing may improve safety and retained speed.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The extension provides plausible controls but no force, impulse, posture-time, or impact model to establish feasibility.

validation_refs: No athlete-run trajectory, rotation, or landing data are supplied.
models.computational_cost: Closed-form scenario formulas plus qualitative discussion.
strengths: Explicitly restores athlete agency after a transparent objective-factors baseline.
limitations: The velocity-conversion case lacks a force or impulse mechanism.
Posture-dependent rotation is not integrated.
Landing choice is not dynamically evaluated.

models.section: Question 1 local effects and bounded geometry search
models.family: parameter sweep and box-constrained design search
models.purpose: Study individual geometry/path effects and select width, height, flat, slope, and takeoff-path parameters for vertical air.
models.summary: The paper defines vertical air as a function of course and path, holds other values at defaults for local response plots, then enumerates a bounded five-variable design domain before optimizing transition shape separately.

variables.definition: Distance between coping edges.
Vertical distance between coping and flat bottom.
Length of the central flat bottom.
Angle between the downhill z axis and horizontal plane.
Path coordinate immediately before flight.
Maximum vertical distance above the coping.

governing_equations.source_expression: max VerticalAir(x,y(x),z(x)) subject to x=y(y), z=z(x) as printed
governing_equations.purpose: State vertical air as the design objective over course and rider path.

equation_status.reason: The page-20 objective is printed schematically rather than as a complete mathematical program; box bounds are given in prose on page 23.

objectives: Maximize vertical air while examining retained energy and practical factor effects.
constraints: W in 13-18 m
H in 2-6 m
B in 4-6 m
zt in 0-15 m
theta in 15-20 degrees
transition shape initially standard ellipse

details: Default W=15 m, H=3.5 m, B=5 m, zt=10 m, theta=18 degrees.
Search-box bounds are stated and several selected values occur at bounds.
Each candidate runs a transient cycle model.

parameter_estimation.method: Design variables are enumerated rather than statistically estimated.

steps: pass fixed dimensions to transition optimization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Grid resolution, combination rule for Vertical Air and E_leave, and exhaustive-search proof are omitted.

assumptions: One-factor sweeps are interpreted with all other variables fixed.
Athlete path is represented through zt.
The physical model from earlier sections owns each objective evaluation.

identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The design box is explicit, but construction, minimum-radius, load, and run-length constraints are deferred and not fed back into this search.

models.computational_cost: Unreported number of deterministic simulations across local sweeps and a bounded enumeration.
strengths: Separates local interpretability from a later joint search and prints all five search ranges.
limitations: Several selected values are search bounds.
No combination rule is stated for the two discussed criteria.
Deferred practical constraints are absent from the feasible set.

models.family: stochastic convex-curve generation and genetic optimization
models.purpose: Search flexible convex transition curves for vertical air, initial angular momentum, total rotation, and later hybrid score.
models.summary: A random increment representation generates monotone convex samples between fixed endpoints; sampled coordinates form genes; the physical objective is fitness; roulette selection, uniform crossover, and random mutation evolve the population.

variables.definition: Number of sampled transition points.
Uniform spacing W/N in the printed generator.
Positive random increments accumulated to generate y samples.
Sampled transition height at x(n).
Vertical air, Lz0, total rotation, or predicted score for a candidate curve.

governing_equations.source_expression: given h=0.01, W=(width-flat)/2, H=Height; x(n)=nh, n=1...N, N=W/h+1
governing_equations.purpose: Discretize the transition domain.

governing_equations.source_expression: goal: y=y(x)={(x(n),y(n))}; subject to y(n)>y(n-1), y(1)=0, y(N)=H
governing_equations.purpose: State monotonicity and endpoint constraints for the sampled transition.
Impose increasing positive increments as the paper's discrete convexity condition.

governing_equations.source_expression: sum_i=2^N k(i) h = y(N)=H implies sum_i=2^N k(i)=H/h
governing_equations.purpose: Normalize increments to reach the endpoint height.

governing_equations.source_expression: After normalized by H/sum_i k(i), acquire k(i); locations are determined and the sampling points of a random convex curve are acquired.
governing_equations.purpose: Reconstruct a candidate curve from normalized random increments.

equation_status.reason: The discrete generator equations on pages 24-25 were visually checked; the final cumulative reconstruction is normalized from the prose and printed summation.

objectives: Maximize the selected physical or hybrid fitness over admissible transition samples.
constraints: Fixed coping and bottom endpoints
Monotone increasing y samples
Increasing positive increments as discrete convexity
Smooth connection is claimed but not fully encoded

details: A random initial generation of curves is shown.
y1=0 and yN=H at fixed horizontal endpoints.
The stochastic optimizer seeks a finite-generation best individual.

parameter_estimation.method: This is a design optimizer rather than parameter inference.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Population size, generation count, operator probabilities, seed, stopping rule, and repeated-run distribution are omitted.

assumptions: Discrete increment monotonicity yields an acceptable convex transition.
The best sampled individual represents the optimum within the unstated stochastic protocol.
A visual second-order curve fit is an adequate interpretation.

strengths: Searches a flexible shape family before fitting an interpretable ellipse-like surrogate.
limitations: The discrete generator and smoothness claim are not fully reconciled.
The stochastic protocol is not reproducible.
The ellipse fits have no residual metric.

models.section: Question 2: airtime, angular momentum, and total rotation design
models.purpose: Tailor course shape separately for airtime, initial angular momentum, and their total-rotation combination.
models.summary: The paper first sweeps geometry for airtime, then maximizes the Lz0 proxy by transition shape, and finally treats total rotation as angular velocity times airtime with angular velocity proportional to angular momentum.

variables.definition: Total duration of flight.
Course-controlled initial angular momentum proxy.
Angular velocity assumed proportional to L0.
Total degree of rotation during flight.

governing_equations.source_expression: L_z0 = sqrt(x_t^2+y_t^2)/(3 rho_0) l^2 m
governing_equations.purpose: Reuse the course-controlled angular-momentum proxy as a shape objective.

governing_equations.source_expression: Theta = omega t_f
governing_equations.purpose: Define total degree of rotation as airborne angular velocity times flight duration.

governing_equations.source_expression: omega proportional to L0
governing_equations.purpose: Link initial angular momentum to the angular velocity used in the total-rotation objective.

Lz0 search uses FIS-like fixed dimensions
Total-rotation search fixes W=15 m and H=3.5 m

details: Each nested optimization uses reported fixed/default geometry before transition search.
The reported airtime solution includes several search-bound values.
Performance is evaluated over one transient cycle and flight.

parameter_estimation.method: Course variables are optimized, not inferred.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: No stochastic convergence or consistency across nested objectives is reported.

assumptions: Angular velocity is proportional to initial angular momentum.
Moment of inertia is effectively fixed in the total-rotation objective.
Separately optimized criteria can inform course tailoring.

models.section: Tailor the course: empirical hybrid scoring and practical tradeoffs
models.family: empirical weighted objective and qualitative practical decision model
models.purpose: Combine airtime and average rotation into one predicted-score objective, then compare the selected course with retained energy, radius, flat, and finite-cycle considerations.
models.summary: An external athlete-scoring regression is imported as genetic-algorithm fitness; the resulting curve is interpreted as a blend of single-objective ellipse-like shapes; practical design is then discussed through radius, flat bottom, E_reach, and cycle count without a final constrained rerun.

variables.definition: Average airtime term in the imported score equation.
